name: t27-lamb-labs ternary MAC co-design benchmark
purpose: Machine-readable state/action/reward definition for an automated ternary model-hardware co-design loop on a Kria-class FPGA. This is the BENCHMARK CONTRACT; it is not an RL agent and not a trained policy.
not_an_rl_system: No state-action-reward LOOP exists yet. This file defines the interface such a loop would use. Calling the current work 'RL' would be false.

state.description: Architecture + quantisation parameters of a candidate design.

schema.arch: enum { ternary_mac, ternary_mac_closed_loop, attention_kv, attention_kv_seq, attention_kv_token }
schema.act_bits: int, activation width (bits); the KV cache stores sign + quant_w magnitude bits of this width
schema.clock: enum { cfgmclk, ring_osc }; cfgmclk is the specified source (~66 MHz family nominal), ring_osc is estimated (~150 MHz) and only structurally verified

action.description: One allowed, single-parameter change to the state.
action.constraint: exactly one field changes per action; every action must be inside the declared domain

reward.definition: negative normalised J/token, subject to a quality floor and a resource constraint

reference.name: closed-loop ternary MAC, 32-bit accumulator
reference.note: Derived from estimated power (0.7 W) / measured tok/s (5.7). When measured power lands, the reference is re-measured and the normalisation is updated.

quality_floor.meaning: the candidate must remain bit-exact against the CPU golden

resource_constraint.rationale: the combinational attention form measured 28,619 LCs = 21.3% of the device and was rejected; the benchmark caps candidates at 10% of the LUT fabric
resource_constraint.note: The combinational attention form measured 28,619 LCs = 21.3% and was rejected. The sequential form measures 455 LCs = 0.34% for the same configuration, so the cap no longer binds for any configuration in the measured sweep.

measurements: estimated_lcs, luts, ffs, bram_36k, dsp48e1, carry4, muxf7, muxf8
tok_per_s (measured on the board, 5 cycle-1 runs)
reproducible_protocol.hash_requirements: every candidate produces a SHA256 of its netlist, its stats log and its quality log; a result without the hash is not accepted
reproducible_protocol.repeat_policy: 5 cycle-1 runs per candidate; report mean, stddev and CV

already_evaluated_states.decision: ACCEPT but saves only 1 LUT / 1 FF
REJECT: quality floor violated (80% mean relative error)
REJECT: quality floor violated (95% mean relative error). Supersedes the resource-only preference in iteration 1.
REJECT by the 10% cap; valid lossless point
REJECT: lossless but wasteful (cache stores 2 bits more than the data needs)
ACCEPT: cheapest lossless configuration, 7.9% of the device LUT fabric, inside the 10% cap
ACCEPT: 0.27% of device, exact 10 cycles/token, verified identical to the combinational golden
ACCEPT: 0.38% of device, exact 18 cycles/token, verified identical to the combinational golden
ACCEPT: 0.28% of device, exact 10 cycles/token, silicon-specified clock
ACCEPT: 0.35% of device, exact 18 cycles/token, silicon-specified clock (reference design)

co_design_rule: The KV cache stores sign + quant_w magnitude bits of an act_bits-wide signed value, so losslessness requires quant_w >= act_bits. QUANT_W is not an independent lever: narrowing it alone is lossy, narrowing act_bits alone at quant_w=8 wastes cache bits. The two must move together.

open_source_engagement.trigger: a Lamb Labs open model appears with a public model card and a licence that permits reproduction and derivative publication
steps: read and record the licence and model card; stop if redistribution or derivatives are forbidden
reproduce the released baseline on CPU (then GPU) and record the golden outputs, tok/s, latency p50/p95
apply the same ternary recipe and sweep ACT_BITS and QUANT_W, recording output agreement, quality metric, AX7203 resources and DRAM reads/token
publish with the same evidence protocol: evidence/<experiment>/ + ARTIFACT_HASHES.txt + a JSON report separating MEASURED / ESTIMATED / TARGET + the validator extended
state the forbidden claims explicitly: no production readiness, no MPU parity, no TinyLlama on Kria, no unhashed figures, no 27B comparison beyond the normalised per-parameter label
open_source_engagement.known_gap: step 3 assumes the released model loads into the local harness; a custom architecture or non-public format turns step 3 into a re-implementation task and the protocol must be amended before running

ring_osc.source: 20-stage fabric inverter chain with a BUFG in the clock path
ring_osc.status: ESTIMATED; the loop is VERIFIED CLOSED in the shipped netlist by evidence/clock/verify_ring_oscillator.py, but FUNCTIONAL oscillation is unverified on silicon

chipdb.status: BUILT AND VERIFIED against the SSOT's size and md5

board_reference.important_correction: The earlier shipped ternary_mac_demo_top_200t.bit drives R23/T23, which the SSOT records as Wukong pins that the AX7203 routes elsewhere. The AX7203's user LEDs are B13/C13/D14/D15, so that bitstream's LED observations are not evidence about this board.

clock_shortfall.status: REPLACED BY A MEASURED CLOCK REFERENCE
clock_shortfall.what_was_claimed: iterations 6 and 7 claimed a 3x shortfall against the board's 200 MHz and blamed the KV read mux
clock_shortfall.why_withdrawn: the same byte-identical netlist measured 45.13, 48.98, 57.30, 71.86 and 73.15 MHz across five seed/router combinations - a 62% spread - so nextpnr's reported Fmax is placement noise on this design, not a measure of logic depth

direct_tests.reading: removing the path iteration 7 blamed made the reported number WORSE, and the BRAM version was IDENTICAL

clock_shortfall.what_survives: the resource numbers (LUT/FF/BRAM/DSP), the quality metric, the combinational-vs-sequational comparison and the lossless rule are stable across seeds
clock_shortfall.what_is_needed: a Vivado timing report or a silicon measurement against the AX7203's 200 MHz oscillator
clock_shortfall.consequence: no tok/s or J/token figure may be derived from a nextpnr-reported Fmax
clock_shortfall.note: the design must be timed against 67.16 MHz measured (CFGMCLK) or 200 MHz (the board oscillator, still unmeasured) - NOT against an estimated 150 MHz fabric oscillator

failures_observed: No wire found for port O6 on source cell (LUT6)
Found two arcs with same sink wire (2D register array with a dynamic index)
Wire ... used as source and sink in different nets: $PACKER_GND_NET$legal$... (a constant net and a real net on one wire)
openxc7_packer_defect.action: Vivado, a patched nextpnr, or a LUT4/constant-net constrained variant. The FPGA flow is part of the design space.

bram_note: the KV cache sits in fabric with 0 BRAM in the register-file implementation; moving it to block RAM costs 1 RAMB36 of 365 and leaves the reported Fmax identical. The 'BRAM = 0' figure is a property of the register implementation, not of the architecture.

cfgmclk_mhz.method: BSCANE2 USER1 readback of a 20-bit ripple counter clocked from STARTUPE2.CFGMCLK, prescaled by 2^8

board_oscillator_r4_t4_mhz.status: MEASURED - the divide ratio was established experimentally before publication

control.purpose: the same design with CFGMCLK in place of the R4/T4 oscillator; the netlists are cell-identical apart from the clock primitive and one output buffer
control.conclusion: the control agrees with the independently measured CFGMCLK (67.16 MHz, ripple prescaler), so JOHNSON_DIVIDE_RATIO = 256 is CONFIRMED

ratio_argument.note: both probes use the SAME chain, so the ratio of their readings IS the ratio of their clocks, independent of the chain's divide ratio

board_oscillator_r4_t4_mhz.documentation_discrepancy: the parent repository's HARDWARE_SSOT.md and docs/fpga/clocking.md record a '200 MHz oscillator on R4/T4'. The measurement says ~398 MHz, about twice that. The measurement is repeatable and the ratio argument is independent of the instrument. WHY the documentation says 200 MHz is recorded as UNKNOWN: the board may run a ~400 MHz oscillator, the SSOT's pin assignment may refer to a different board revision, or the documented value may be a nominal the board does not run at.

fabric_ring_oscillator.status: CONFIRMED NOT OSCILLATING - controlled pair run back-to-back in one session: 30 reads over 15 s with the counter never moving, while the CFGMCLK control of the identical design counted correctly at 66.85 MHz. Two independent CFGMCLK runs agree to 0.5% (67.16, 66.85 MHz).

die_telemetry.method: openFPGALoader --read-xadc over JTAG, 5 readings 2 s apart
die_telemetry.explicit_non_claim: this is NOT a power measurement: the XADC senses voltage and temperature, not current, and the XC7A200T has no on-die current sensor. POWER_WATTS and J/token remain ESTIMATED.

toolchain_workarounds.openxc7_lut6_packer_defect: BYPASSED - restrict the ABC mapping to `abc -lut 2` instead of the stock `abc -luts 2:2,3,6:5`; with no LUT6 in the netlist the 'No wire found for port O6' failure disappears
toolchain_workarounds.carry_chain_routing_failure: AVOIDED - a plain flip-flop ripple counter has no CARRY4; openXC7's placer splits CARRY4 chains across non-adjacent slices
toolchain_workarounds.bscane2_user1_readback: WORKS over the Digilent HS2: 6-bit IR (USER1 = 0x02), framing TLR(5) -> RTI -> Select-DR -> Select-IR -> Capture-IR -> Shift-IR -> 6 IR bits -> Update-IR -> RTI, then RTI -> Select-DR -> Capture-DR -> Shift-DR
toolchain_workarounds.openfpgaloader_xadc_json: emits JSON with a trailing comma, which is not valid JSON - parse the fields with a regex

published_throughput.reason: the only published figure (~5.7 tok/s) came from bitstream/ternary_mac_demo_top_200t.bit, which has two defects verified from its netlist: every flip-flop is clocked by the fabric ring oscillator (which does not oscillate), and synthesis pruned the 32-bit accumulator to 2 bits because acc_in is constant 0 and w_code is constant -1
published_throughput.variance_gate: REOPENED - the accumulator_final values in evidence/variance_summary.json cannot have come from that bitstream
published_throughput.what_is_needed: a design whose clock runs: the AX7203's 200 MHz differential oscillator on R4/T4 (needs a pin-bearing probe) or CFGMCLK at ~67 MHz measured

still_open: publish no tok/s until a design with a running clock is measured
measure the AX7203's 200 MHz differential oscillator on R4/T4 with a pin-bearing probe
redo the variance gate on a design whose clock runs
FPGA power and J/token: still ESTIMATED, a current meter in series with the rail is required
the sequential attention design still does not route in openXC7

attention_resource_correction.status: PUBLISHED - the committed attention module's KV cache was dead; the corrected module is VERIFIED
defects_found_in_the_committed_rtl: the cache was declared with one dimension and indexed with two, so synthesis pruned it away
a flat packed vector written with a variable-offset part-select is not synthesizable as a register file - yosys drops the write while the simulation still passes
the score carried a factor-of-16 padding that overflowed its 17-bit accumulator, so the score's sign was wrong
the key magnitude was held in a QUANT_W-bit SIGNED register, so magnitudes >= 2^(QUANT_W-1) came out negative
the accumulator addition was UNSIGNED, because a Verilog part-select is always unsigned
attention_resource_correction.co_design_finding: the cache IMPLEMENTATION is a first-class decision: distributed RAM 2763 LCs and zero BRAM, block RAM 2934 LCs and 6 RAMB18E1, registers 18695 LCs and no RAM. Only the register form misses the 10% cap.
attention_resource_correction.verification: VERIFIED - Verilator against a CPU golden, 10 configurations x 120 randomised trials = 1200 trials, 0 mismatches. Verilator rather than Icarus because Icarus accepted the variable-offset write that yosys drops.
attention_resource_correction.throughput_attempt: ATTEMPTED - the token-rate probe does not route in openXC7: block RAM 'No wire found for port A6', distributed RAM 'port DI2', registers the placer scattered the BSCANE2 shift register over 36 seeds. No throughput number is published.
